simple.meaning: קִיקָלוֹן (qîyqâlôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “intense disgrace.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Habakkuk 2:16. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קִיקָלוֹן (H7022) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: קִיקָלוֹן (qîyqâlôwn) / H7022 is traced through Habakkuk 2:16 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H7022. qiqalon קִיקָלוֺן noun [masculine] disgrace ; — Hab 2:16 , si vera lectio intensive Ol § 82 c Kö ii. 130, 497 , but dubious (see We Now GASm).

occurrences.englishText: You are filled with shame, and not glory. You will also drink, and be exposed! The cup of Yahweh’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
